swatow.summary: A telegram signed 'Tanaka' from Swatow to Sun Yat-sen's household in Tokyo, intercepted by the Japanese Foreign Ministry, which could not read it. It reports that Mo Qingyu declared Chaozhou independent against Yuan Shikai, that Sun's men recovered Swatow, and that Mo then came with a large force and ordered them out of the garrison headquarters.
swatow.en:
Chaozhou city has declared independence under Mo Qingyu. Our army too has recovered Swatow. Afterwards Mo came with a
large body of troops and ordered us out of the garrison headquarters. Our army's strength is weak; for the time being we
are holding on with the support of 翼□. Wenhui returns to [?Hong Kong] … [last word garbled]. (Tanaka)

dudout-shanghai1916.summary: Shanghai ↔ Tokyo (“Rosamonde”, Yamada Junzaburō), June 1915–April 1916. Table published by D. Bourdeau. Also attested from Changchun on 31 July 1914.
dudout-shanghai1916.en:
The representative will undertake it on returning. Please come within […] days to discuss the funds […]. Indicator “Ting”, sender unidentified.

Have the funds been received? — Sun Wen.

Received the rest; one must be careful in everything. — Mei (美, Chen Qimei).

Zhongyuan (Deng Keng) is waiting for funds; he leaves at once for Shanghai. Can you raise ten thousand yuan? Li's intentions are not yet clear; do not worry.

Lin Dexuan is coming by a French ship: please meet him at the boat.

For Yingshi's (Chen Qimei's) illness, the best is to have him treated by Dr Takano's method. I myself have long suffered from my stomach and was treated many times without effect; recently I tried Dr Takano's method and his diet, and was at once completely [cured?]. But whenever I take a little tea, coffee, […] or meat, the illness comes back.

dudout-yamada1916.summary: Tokyo ↔ Shanghai (“Junzaburo”, “Linwailuk”), May–June 1916; clear indicator “Thirtyseventh” on most. Table published by D. Bourdeau.
dudout-yamada1916.en:
Arrived safely in Shanghai? […] the Jiangmen letter was received, but the reply was lost (?). The representatives of San Francisco (金山) and Los Angeles (羅省) […], Ma Xing […], three people, arrived in Japan yesterday: can they be urged to go to Shanghai? [Wang] Zhaoming means to find Du Shi to help draft the bonds; ask brother [Liao] Zhongkai whether he can see to it. — The 3rd.

[…]qiu is taking the Hakuai-maru to Shanghai. — Chi. […]

Shao Zifeng telegraphs: at Huairen, Wang Huanxia on 28 April led [the troops of] two districts, [Huairen] and […], five hundred [men], who declared themselves independent (獨立); but their forces having been defeated (?), he plans to move men and arms along the Yalu to the Andong concession, recruit several thousand more and await orders. Move them on to another province; reply quickly,” etc. Instructions requested: reply.

dudout-seito1916.summary: Qingdao ↔ Tokyo (Ju Zheng, Kayano Nagatomo), March–April 1916. Table published by D. Bourdeau.
dudout-seito1916.en:
Notes: one million yuan, to be stamped; requisition receipts and three-part pledge forms: once printed (?), send them quickly.

[Our] two telegrams of the 25th and the 26th await a reply. Needs here are very urgent: let us know quickly. As soon as Du (杜) has arrived (?), be sure to send by telegraphic transfer. — Zheng (Ju Zheng). The 28th.

We will do our utmost to raise the 50,000: you can start quickly. Also examine in detail whether, since the abolition of the monarchy, the troops intend to withdraw; reply at once.

[The method (?)] for dealing with […] is duly received. Here, one stroke could lead straight to […] Jinan (?); only 50,000 yuan is needed: please send it quickly by telegraphic transfer. [We] hope for a telegraphic reply the same day.

Brother Liao (presumably Liao Zhongkai): one million yuan in military notes, send quickly. Reply.

dudout-manila1916.summary: Tokyo ↔ Manila, March 1916. Table published by D. Bourdeau.
dudout-manila1916.en:
There is nothing of the sort. — Wen, replying.

Tan Gen has arrived in Manila; he is taking aeroplanes to support Long Jiguang and leaves Manila tomorrow. What should be done? Reply urgently. — Ying.

Bacon (倍根) […] has not written a receipt: it is feared that this has no value in law. There is no need to sue him; we can only [press for payment (?)] on simple common sense. See how he replies; we will then find other means.

The Uncle telegraphs that Fujian still needs funds: raise some and remit them to Japan, for transfer to Shanghai; also have Iloilo (怡朗) informed. — Wen (Sun Yat-sen).

Who is using our code to telegraph from Shanghai? The instruction to hand 50,000 to Yamada (山田) in Shanghai is suspicious. From now on, use the code left by Zhantang (Hu Hanmin). — Ying.

Please draw 4,000 yuan at the HSBC. Reply. — Ying.

[…] Telegram: southern Fujian will soon declare independence.

dudout-sanfran1916.summary: San Francisco → “Dr Sunwen”, Tokyo, October 1915–April 1916; signed 森 (Lin Sen). Table published by D. Bourdeau. Also attested on 18 September 1914.
dudout-sanfran1916.en:
My funds are exhausted while travelling; send two hundred US dollars urgently. On the [15th], ten thousand yuan were sent to Japan: have you received them? Reply on this too.

The five-yuan [bonds] sell easily; send many quickly.

Bought two aircraft, price 40,000 in gold. Deng returns first. Send the bonds and merit medals quickly. — Sen (Lin Sen).

Telegram received; twenty thousand remitted […]. […] returns on the same ship as Deng. The aircraft can […] in two months. Bonds […] received. Lin Sen. Exact day unreadable.

The situation worsens daily. Yuan […] independence to counter the revolutionaries […]. Unless I enter the country myself, I fear our party cannot build a strong force. I therefore decide to return on the 27th. Send the aircraft and comrades back quickly, and remit spare funds urgently. Xie Chi will act for the Tokyo headquarters;

dudout-honolulu1916.summary: Honolulu → Tokyo, 30 April and 16 May 1916; indicator “Aloha”. Grid published by D. Bourdeau, written here with an alphabet without q and with w (23 October 2026).
dudout-honolulu1916.en:
Huang (黃, Huang Xing) and Deng (鄧) arrive in Japan and change ship there for Shanghai. — Tiecheng (鐵城, Wu Tiecheng).

I cannot go to Jin (金, Jinshan, San Francisco?); I am returning home at once. How are things since your arrival in Shanghai? […] reply by telegram. — Tiecheng (鐵城, Wu Tiecheng).

snip.cap: The Swatow telegram to Sun Yat-sen, 3 April 1916

system: Standard Chinese telegraph code condensed to consonant-vowel syllables by a systematic table (20 consonants rotated to l, vowels e a i o u, column-major 01-00), no additive.
